# YouTube Partner Program Requirements Explained (500 vs 1,000 Subscribers)

Source: https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/blog/youtube-partner-program-requirements-explained/
Published: 2026-10-04 | Updated: 2026-10-18 | Site: Creator Toolkit (free YouTube creator tools)
Related free tool: Monetization Progress tracker - https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#monetization

**TL;DR:** YouTube has two entry levels. In eligible countries you can apply at 500 subscribers, 3 public uploads in 90 days and 3,000 watch hours (or 3 million Shorts views) for fan funding features. Ad revenue sharing needs 1,000 subscribers plus 4,000 watch hours in 12 months or 10 million Shorts views in 90 days. The Monetization Progress tracker shows how close you are to each.

Most creators ask the same thing early on: how many subscribers and hours do I need before I can earn money? The answer has two parts now, and the numbers depend on your country. This page uses YouTube's own help pages, read on the date at the bottom.

## The two tiers

| | Fan funding tier (expanded program) | Full tier (ad revenue sharing) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Subscribers | 500 | 1,000 |
| Uploads | 3 valid public uploads in the last 90 days | Not part of the headline threshold |
| Watch time | 3,000 qualified watch hours in the last 12 months | 4,000 qualified watch hours in the last 12 months |
| Or Shorts views | 3 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days | 10 million qualified Shorts views in the last 90 days |
| What you get | Earlier access to fan funding and Shopping features | Revenue sharing from ads and YouTube Premium, plus the other features |

Source: YouTube's pages on the [expanded Partner Program](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13429240) and the [Partner Program overview](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851). You need to meet either the watch hours route or the Shorts views route, not both.

The 500 subscriber tier is only for creators in the countries YouTube lists on its expanded program page. If your country is not on that list, YouTube says there are no changes for you, so the 1,000 subscriber rules apply.

## What counts as a "qualified" hour or view?

YouTube counts only certain watch time. For example, its overview page says qualified watch hours from Shorts views in the Shorts feed do not count towards the 4,000 hour threshold. Likewise, the Shorts route needs qualified views on public Shorts. The exact definitions are in a collapsed section of the [overview page](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851), so check that section against your own numbers in YouTube Studio. The tracker cannot see inside your account, so it only does arithmetic on what you type.

## Other requirements besides the numbers

Hitting the numbers is not enough. YouTube's overview lists these as well:

- Follow the channel monetization policies.
- Live in a country or region where the program is available.
- Have no active Community Guidelines strikes.
- Turn on 2-Step Verification on your Google Account.
- Have advanced features access.
- Link one active AdSense for YouTube account, or set one up in Studio when you apply.

## How to check if your channel can apply

1. Open YouTube Studio and look at the **Earn** area. It shows your own eligibility and has a Get notified option.
2. Write down your subscribers, your public watch hours for the last 12 months, and your Shorts views for the last 90 days from Analytics.
3. Enter them in the [Monetization Progress tracker](https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#monetization) to see the percentage for each tier.
4. Check the non-number requirements above, especially strikes and 2-Step Verification.
5. When you are eligible, choose **Apply now** in the Earn area.

## What happens after you apply

YouTube says an application goes to automated systems and human reviewers who look at the channel as a whole. A decision typically takes about a month, and delays are possible. If you are turned down, the help page says you can try again after a waiting period (30 days for a first rejection, 90 days after that) and should review your channel against the policies first.

One more point from the same page: YouTube may turn off monetization on channels that have not uploaded a video or posted to the Posts tab for six months or more.

## A note on changes

YouTube's overview page currently shows a notice about updated Partner Program terms starting February 1, 2027, with creators asked to accept the updated terms in Studio by January 31, 2027. Rules change, so treat any article, including this one, as a snapshot and check the Earn tab for your own channel.

## What the tracker does not do

- It does not know your real numbers. You type them in.
- It does not check your country, strikes, 2-Step Verification or AdSense link.
- It does not predict when you will reach the goal or promise that you will.
- It does not check whether your watch hours are "qualified". Use the figure YouTube Studio gives you.

## FAQ

### How many subscribers do you need to monetize on YouTube?
In countries where the expanded program is available, 500 subscribers (with 3 public uploads in 90 days and 3,000 watch hours or 3 million Shorts views) gives access to fan funding features. For ad revenue sharing you need 1,000 subscribers with 4,000 watch hours in 12 months or 10 million Shorts views in 90 days.

### Do I need 4,000 watch hours and 10 million Shorts views?
No. It is one or the other. Pick the route that matches how your channel gets its views.

### Do Shorts watch hours count towards 4,000 hours?
YouTube says qualified watch hours from Shorts views in the Shorts feed do not count towards the 4,000 hour threshold. Shorts have their own 10 million view route.

### How long does the review take?
YouTube says it is typically about one month, and it can take longer when volumes are high.

### Can I buy views or subscribers to qualify?
No. YouTube's fake engagement rules prohibit it, and bought numbers can get a channel removed. The tracker has no feature to buy anything.

## Sources

- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72851
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/13429240
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9314357

---
From Creator Toolkit: https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/

# YouTube Title Ideas That Work Without Clickbait

Source: https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/blog/youtube-title-ideas-that-are-not-clickbait/
Published: 2026-10-03 | Updated: 2026-10-18 | Site: Creator Toolkit (free YouTube creator tools)
Related free tool: Title and Tag Ideas generator - https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#titles

**TL;DR:** A good title tells the right viewer what they get, uses the words they would actually search, and keeps the main phrase near the front. The Title and Tag Ideas tool gives you ten angles and a starter set of tags for any topic. Treat the output as a first draft and rewrite it to match your real video.

A title has two jobs. It has to match what a viewer is searching for, and it has to make the right person want to click. The [Title and Tag Ideas tool](https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#titles) helps with the first draft. This guide explains how to pick a good one and fix a weak one.

## What YouTube says about search

YouTube's [search help page](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16090438) says ranking looks at relevance, engagement and quality. For relevance it looks at how well the title, tags, description and the video content match the search. So the title matters, but it is only one signal. Nobody outside YouTube can tell you the exact weight of each part, and anyone who claims to is guessing.

## How to write a YouTube title from a topic

1. Start with the plain topic in words a viewer would type. "Indoor gardening for beginners" is better than a clever phrase nobody searches.
2. Pick an angle. Is this a how-to, a list, a mistake, a comparison, a story or a result? The angle is the reason to click.
3. Put the main phrase early. Long titles get cut off in search results and on phones, so the words at the front do the most work.
4. Keep it under 100 characters. That is YouTube's hard limit for a title, per its [video settings page](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57404). Staying near 60 is a safer habit so little gets cut.
5. Check the promise. Read the title, then read your first 30 seconds. If the video does not deliver what the title says, change the title.

## Ten title angles that work

The tool fills these patterns with your topic:

- **The hidden part:** "[Topic]: What Nobody Tells You"
- **The step by step:** "How to [Topic] (Step by Step)"
- **The test:** "I Tried [Topic] for 30 Days - Honest Results"
- **The time box:** "[Topic] Explained in Under 10 Minutes"
- **The myth bust:** "The Truth About [Topic]"
- **The mistakes list:** "7 [Topic] Mistakes Beginners Always Make"
- **The fix:** "Why Your [Topic] Isn't Working (and How to Fix It)"
- **The starter:** "[Topic] for Beginners: Start Here"
- **The pause:** "Before You Start [Topic], Watch This"
- **The guide:** "[Topic] in 2026: The Complete Guide"

Only use a pattern if it is true. "I Tried it for 30 Days" is only a title if you did.

## Clickbait is a real risk, not just a style problem

YouTube's [spam and deceptive practices policy](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801973) lists malicious clickbait: titles, thumbnails or descriptions that trick people into clicking on a video that does not deliver what it promised. YouTube's own [click-through rate help](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7628154) also says clickbait videos tend to have low average view duration, so they are less likely to be recommended. A title that overpromises can win the click and lose the video.

## What about the tags?

The tool also suggests a starter set of tags. YouTube's [video settings page](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57404) says tags can help when your topic is often misspelled, and otherwise "play a minimal role in your video's discovery." So do not spend an hour on them. Add the main topic and common misspellings, then move on. For more on this, see the [tags guide](https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/blog/youtube-tags-extractor-do-tags-matter/).

## Limits of a title generator

- It uses templates. It does not know your video, your audience or your niche, so some results will sound off. Delete those.
- It cannot predict views, ranking or click-through rate.
- It does not check what is already ranking. For that, use [keyword suggestions](https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/blog/youtube-keyword-research-with-autocomplete/) and look at the search results yourself.

## FAQ

### How long should a YouTube title be?
YouTube allows up to 100 characters. Many creators aim for roughly 60 or fewer so the whole title shows on phones and in search results. That 60 figure is a common habit, not a YouTube rule.

### Do keywords in the title help?
Yes, relevance is one thing YouTube says it looks at, and the title is one of the places it checks. Use the words a viewer would actually type, and write it for a person first.

### Are numbers in titles better?
Not always. A number can make a promise concrete, such as "7 mistakes". It is a choice, not a requirement.

### Can a title generator guarantee more views?
No. No tool can. A title helps people understand the video and decide to click. Views depend on the video, the audience and what YouTube chooses to recommend.

### Should I change the title of an old video?
You can, but change one thing at a time so you can see the effect. YouTube also has a Test and Compare feature in Studio that can test up to three titles and thumbnails on eligible videos.

## Sources

- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/16090438
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/57404
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/7628154
- https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/2801973

From Creator Toolkit: https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/

# How to Download a YouTube Thumbnail in Every Size

Source: https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/blog/how-to-download-youtube-thumbnails/
Published: 2026-10-02 | Updated: 2026-10-18 | Site: Creator Toolkit (free YouTube creator tools)
Related free tool: Thumbnail Grabber - https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#thumbnails

**TL;DR:** Paste a YouTube link into the Thumbnail Grabber and it lists every thumbnail size YouTube has for that video, from 320 x 180 up to the 1280 x 720 max resolution file, so you can save the one you need. If you are making your own, YouTube recommends 3840 x 2160 pixels in JPG or PNG with a 16:9 shape.

Every public YouTube video has a thumbnail image stored in several sizes. You can save any of them without a screenshot. The Creator Toolkit [Thumbnail Grabber](https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#thumbnails) shows all of them for a link you paste, so you can pick the size you want and download it.

## What sizes does YouTube keep?

YouTube stores a thumbnail for each video at a few fixed sizes. These are the ones the grabber lists:

| Size name | Dimensions | Good for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Max resolution | 1280 x 720 | Blog headers, presentations, reviewing a design |
| Standard | 640 x 480 | Medium previews |
| High | 480 x 360 | Small embeds |
| Medium | 320 x 180 | Tiny previews and lists |

The max resolution file does not exist for every video. If a video was uploaded in lower quality, or is very old, YouTube may only have the smaller sizes. The grabber shows what is available and hides what is not.

## How to download a YouTube thumbnail

1. Open the video on YouTube and copy the link from the address bar or the Share button. Watch links, youtu.be links, Shorts links, embed links and plain 11-character video IDs all work.
2. Paste it into the [Thumbnail Grabber](https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#thumbnails) and press **Get thumbnails**.
3. Pick the size you need. Open it in a new tab to check it, or use the download button.
4. If you plan to reuse the image, read the section below first.

## Can you reuse someone else's thumbnail?

Downloading an image is easy. Having the right to use it is a separate question. A thumbnail is usually the creator's artwork, so copying it into your own video or post without permission can be a copyright problem. Good reasons to grab a thumbnail are research, a reference for your own design, or a screenshot for a review where you are allowed to show it. When in doubt, ask the creator.

Also keep in mind that YouTube's [thumbnails policy](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/9229980) does not allow a thumbnail that misleads viewers into thinking they will see something that is not in the video. That applies to the thumbnails you make too.

## What YouTube says about your own thumbnails

Here is what YouTube's [custom thumbnail help page](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/72431) recommends today:

- A resolution of 3840 x 2160 pixels for videos (2160 x 3840 for Shorts), with a minimum width of 640 pixels for videos.
- JPG or PNG files.
- An aspect ratio of 16:9 for videos and 9:16 for Shorts.
- File size limits that depend on the device. Uploads from a computer allow up to 50 MB. Mobile uploads for video thumbnails are limited to 2 MB.
- Uploading a custom thumbnail needs a verified account.

YouTube also says vertical videos that use a 16:9 custom thumbnail get an auto-generated 4:5 thumbnail on the home, explore and subscription pages. Your own thumbnail still shows in other places, such as the watch feed and on desktop.

## Tips for checking a thumbnail before you publish

- Shrink it. Most viewers see your thumbnail at around the size of a postage stamp. If the text is not readable at 320 pixels wide, it is too small.
- Test it against the competition. Put your thumbnail next to videos in the same topic. The [Thumbnail Preview and A/B Compare](https://devanasolver.github.io/youtube-creator-toolkit/#abtest) tool shows it in a mock feed.
- Keep one idea per image. A face, an object and a few big words is plenty.
- Match the promise to the video. A thumbnail that overpromises gets clicks and then people leave, and YouTube's own help says clickbait tends to produce low average view duration.

## Limits of the Thumbnail Grabber

- It only reads public videos. Private and deleted videos have no public thumbnail.
- It shows the thumbnail YouTube currently serves. If the creator changed it recently, you may see the old one for a short time.
- It does not tell you which thumbnail performs better. Only YouTube Studio data can do that.

## FAQ

### How do I download a YouTube thumbnail?
Copy the video link, paste it into the Thumbnail Grabber, press Get thumbnails and save the size you want. No sign-up is needed.

### What is the biggest YouTube thumbnail size I can download?
For most videos it is the 1280 x 720 max resolution file. Some videos only have smaller sizes.

### What size should my own YouTube thumbnail be?
YouTube recommends 3840 x 2160 pixels for videos with a 16:9 aspect ratio, and at least 640 pixels wide. Use JPG or PNG. On a computer the limit is 50 MB.

### Can I get the thumbnail from a Short?
Yes. Paste the Shorts link. Shorts thumbnails are 9:16 when the creator uploaded a custom one, so the images can look different from long videos.

### Is it legal to use another creator's thumbnail?
Downloading is not the problem, reusing is. A thumbnail is normally the creator's work, so ask for permission unless a specific exception applies. This is general information, not legal advice.
